title: ShinyHunters Exploits Oracle PeopleSoft Vulnerability CVE-2026-35273 in New Attack Wave
content_md: ShinyHunters has resumed large-scale attacks against Oracle PeopleSoft , using a small change to its exploit to get past some web application firewall (WAF) rules. Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) say the group, tracked as UNC6240, has deployed web shells on dozens of systems worldwide. The latest targets span higher education, technology, IT services, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government. CVE-2026-35273 affects Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools. Oracle says the flaw can be exploited remotely without authentication and may allow an attacker to run code on a vulnerable server. Oracle lists PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62 as affected and rates the issue 9.8 on the CVSS scale. The company issued an emergency security alert on June 10, 2026. ShinyHunters Renew PeopleSoft Attacks ShinyHunters first exploited the flaw as a zero-day between May 27 and June 9, mainly against universities. In the renewed campaign, the group changed the request path from /PSEMHUB/ to /%50SEMHUB/ . The sequence %50 represents the letter “P.” A WAF rule looking only for the literal /PSEMHUB/ path may miss the encoded request, while the PeopleSoft server decodes it and sends it to the vulnerable Environment Management Hub endpoint. Mandiant observed attackers sending repeated POST requests to /%50SEMHUB/hub to check whether servers were vulnerable.
